takeaways.text: Net sales hit $4,600M, up from $3,850M a year ago, yet net income fell 73% to $109M from $402M. Gross margin narrowed to 9.6% from 15.5% and operating costs rose 34%, so the extra sales did not reach the bottom line.
takeaways.title: Sales grew, but profit fell by nearly three-quarters

takeaways.text: Cost of sales ate $4,160M of the $4,600M in sales, leaving a 9.6% gross margin — down from 15.5% a year ago and 11.8% last quarter. Operating income fell 61% to $147M as R&D jumped 40% YoY to $163M on hiring for next-generation server and rack designs.
takeaways.title: Thin margins are the story

takeaways.text: Some customers delayed platform decisions in the quarter, and Supermicro cut its full-year FY25 revenue guidance to $21.8–22.6B from $23.5–25.0B, though it expects many of those commitments to land in the June and September quarters. Operations still generated $627M of cash, and cash ended March 31 at $2.54B versus $2.49B of bank debt and convertible notes.
takeaways.title: Guidance cut as customers delayed

verdict: Supermicro sold 19.5% more in the quarter, but its thin margins got thinner and profit fell by nearly three-quarters to $109 million as customers delayed big AI platform decisions.
